From: Ben Collins <ben.collins@brightcart.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA proposal questions (BrightCart pilot)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a couple of clarifications on the SLA language before we go to legal: specifically around how uptime credits are applied across regional failovers, and whether the 4-hour P1 response window is guaranteed during our EU maintenance blackout.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether credits are assessed per region or across an account-wide aggregation? We run production in us-west and eu-west and need to understand how credits stack if both regions see brief interruptions.
- We want to include a contingency credit (one-time) if an incident causes multi-region degradation for > 30 minutes during peak; is that something Redwood will consider as part of the pilot pricing?

If helpful I can loop in our procurement mailbox (procurement@brightcart.com) — they prefer a short written addendum rather than a long redline.

—Ben
Head of Infrastructure, BrightCart
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Ben Collins <ben.collins@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA proposal questions (BrightCart pilot)

Ben —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answers up front, then details and a next-step propose: 

1) Credit aggregation: Redwood applies credits at the account level by default (we calculate outage minutes per region and then apply an account-aggregated credit formula). However, for pilots where customers want explicit regional ceilings we can offer per-region crediting as an add-on in the quote. That typically increases the TCV by ~3–6% for dual-region redundancy.

2) Contingency credit: We can include a one-time contingency credit for multi-region degradation > 30m as a pilot concession. We typically limit these to one per billing period and cap at 10% of the monthly invoice for the affected services. For pilots we can negotiate the cap down (BrightCart ask: what cap would you be comfortable with?).

Proposed next step: I will circulate a short addendum that clearly states (a) account vs region crediting option, (b) a contingency credit line with the proposed cap, and (c) an operational handoff for escalation (names and on-call windows). If that looks good, Karthik can attach pricing delta lines and Marissa will prep the runbook excerpt.

Thanks,
Lauren
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben / Lauren / procurement team —

Quick pricing note from my side: if BrightCart wants explicit per-region crediting + a one-time contingency credit we model the delta two ways: (1) one-time pilot concession (no change to standard rates; concession amortized in month 1) or (2) permanent add-on (adds a small premium to recurring fees). For pilot simplicity we recommend option (1) and list the concession in the contract addendum so it doesn't create ongoing precedent.

Suggested numbers:
- Per-region crediting add-on: +4% TCV (covers accounting and reserved capacity buffers)
- Contingency credit cap (pilot): 6% of monthly recurring charges, one-time use during pilot term
- If you prefer a lower cap for adoption reasons, we can set it to 3% but require a 3-month pilot extension to validate signals.

I attached a pricing worksheet with example math. Happy to walk through on a 20-minute call.

—Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

Lauren / Karthik —

Thanks, this is helpful. Procurement is leaning toward the one-time concession approach (option 1) — they dislike ongoing add-ons. Two questions before we sign:

1) If BrightCart triggers the contingency credit, what is the operational playbook? We need clarity on (a) how we escalate (email + PagerDuty), (b) evidence required (incident timeline + metrics), and (c) approval flow for credit issuance.

2) For the 4-hour P1 response window, our EU maintenance blackout is monthly 03:00–04:00 UTC on the second Tuesday. Will Redwood continue to guarantee the 4-hour window during that window or do we need to suppress SLOs for the maintenance window?

Procurement asked me to add that they prefer the addendum to reference the doc by filename rather than embedding long clauses in the main contract.

—Ben

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ben Collins <ben.collins@brightcart.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency crediting & regional escalation handoff

Ben —

Thanks for the clarification. I drafted a short runbook excerpt and the addendum stub (see attached). Key operational points:

- Escalation flow: customer files incident (support@redwood.ai) → automatic PagerDuty paging to on-call SRE (15m) → Tier 2 on-call (45m) → Incident manager review (2h). We will include a named on-call rotation window for BrightCart pilot (US business hours + EU overlap 08:00–16:00 UTC).
- Evidence package: incident ID, aggregated region metrics (error rate, request success), and a 15-minute granularity timeline exported from Redwood Trace. That is normally sufficient for credit evaluation.
- Credit approval: initial credit recommendation by Incident Manager, final signoff from Finance Ops (within 7 business days). Once approved the credit is applied to the next invoice cycle.

Regarding the EU maintenance blackout: we can keep the 4-hour P1 response guarantee active during the blackout provided BrightCart publishes the monthly maintenance window at least 14 days in advance and agrees to a 30-minute maintenance notification window. If the maintenance extends unexpectedly and causes degraded signals outside the advance notice, normal credit rules apply (i.e., a contingency credit could be eligible).

Next steps I propose:
1) Lauren: circulate the single-page addendum that references the attached runbook file (escalation-runbook-draft.docx) and the SLA-quote PDF.
2) Ben / procurement: confirm the preferred contingency cap (6% or 3% + pilot extension).
3) Quick sign-off call if needed — 20 min this week.

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
